options.html: reduces the rate of strength development and leads to higher shrinkage.
increases the rate of strength development and reduces the rate of deterioration.
decreases the rate of strength development and increases the rate of deterioration.
increases the rate of strength development and leads to higher shrinkage.

questions.solution:
(d)
The fineness of cement refers to the particle size of the cement. Finer particles provide a greater
surface area for hydration, leading to the following effects:
• Faster strength development
– Finer cement hydrates more quickly.
– This accelerates early-age strength gain, especially in the first 7 days.
• Increased shrinkage
– Due to increased surface area and faster hydration, the water demand increases.
– As a result, more drying shrinkage occurs.
• Potential durability issues
– If not properly cured, fine cement can lead to development of micro-cracks due to rapid
setting and shrinkage.

Which of the following contracts is most suitable when the labour and material costs are liable to fluctuate heavily in the market i.e. there is uncertainty in the specifications?
questions.solution:
(d)
Cost plus percentage rate contract: In this type of contract, a contractor agrees to take the work
of construction on the actual cost of work plus on agreed percentage in addition, for his services.

market.

If superplasticizers are mixed in concrete then. Which of the following statement(s) is/are correct?

options.html: it increase the compressive strength of concrete.
it enables the use of a lower water-cement ratio, thereby improving compressive strength.
it accelerates the setting time of concrete.
it allows for reduced cement content, thereby increasing compressive strength of concrete.

questions.solution:
(b)
• Superplasticizers don’t directly increase strength.
• Lowering the water-cement ration without affecting workability is one of the primary
functions of super plasticizers. It leads to increased strength.
• Superplasticizers typically increase the setting time (retardation effect), as they delay the
hydration process.
• Superplasticizers don’t inherently increase strength of concrete with reduced cement.
